claim: DriverInitialize wipes the live DRIVER_OBJECT after registering dispatch and unload entry points, so the loaded driver no longer has valid IRP handlers.
evidence: dummy/driver_lifecycle.c:101-107 registers MajorFunction handlers and DriverUnload, then immediately calls RtlZeroMemory(DriverObject, sizeof(DRIVER_OBJECT)). Microsoft documents that the driver object stores the dispatch table and unload routine used after DriverEntry.
runtimeTrigger: Load the driver successfully, then issue a normal CreateFile or DeviceIoControl against the exposed device path. The I/O manager reaches a DRIVER_OBJECT whose MajorFunction entries and DriverUnload pointer were zeroed after initialization.

claim: The new user-visible Global link is created in the wrong object-manager namespace and its creation status is ignored, so both clients can target a path that the driver never actually publishes.
evidence: common/protocol.h:10, controller/controller/transport.c:8-15, and client/DriverApi.cs:74-112 all open \\.\Global\Ki000. But dummy/driver_lifecycle.c:56-58 calls IoCreateSymbolicLink on L"\Global\Ki000" instead of a global MS-DOS name such as \DosDevices\Global\Ki000, and it does not check the return status before reporting success.
runtimeTrigger: Load the driver and run either client. CreateFile targets \\.\Global\Ki000, but if the symbolic link was not created in the MS-DOS namespace the open fails immediately even though DriverInitialize returned STATUS_SUCCESS.
